{"reading": 1, "entries": [{"n": 1, "what": "Arrives in the reception room with Anna Mikháylovna. Prince Vasíli and the eldest princess fall silent; Pierre thinks he sees the princess hide something. Vasíli says nothing to him, only squeezing his arm below the shoulder."}, {"n": 2, "what": "In the small circular drawing room he remembers sitting there during balls, not knowing how to dance, watching ladies multiplied in the mirrors; now two candles, whispering strangers, and he does not eat although he would very much have liked to."}, {"n": 3, "what": "Sees his \"monitress\" go back on tiptoe to the reception room, concludes that this too is essential, and follows after a short interval."}, {"n": 4, "what": "Called into the fight as a witness (\"Pierre, my dear, come here... I think he will not be out of place in a family consultation\"), he comes quite close and gazes in astonishment at the princess' face, which has lost all dignity, and at Prince Vasíli's twitching cheeks. He says nothing — he speaks not one line in this chapter."}, {"n": 5, "what": "The eldest princess comes out of the bedroom, sees him, and turns on him with irrepressible hatred: \"Yes, now you may be glad! This is what you have been waiting for.\""}, {"n": 6, "what": "Prince Vasíli staggers out, drops onto the sofa beside him, takes him by the elbow and weeps about sin, deceit and death, with a sincerity and weakness Pierre had never heard in his voice before."}, {"n": 7, "what": "Anna Mikháylovna comes out last, kisses his forehead, wets him with her tears and tells him \"He is no more.\" She leads him into the dark drawing room, where he is glad no one can see his face, and returns to find him asleep with his head on his arm."}, {"n": 8, "what": "In the morning she tells him he is young and now, she hopes, in command of an immense fortune — but that the will has NOT yet been opened — and asks him to carry out his father's wish about Borís.
